result:
`validateApp` now throws if `owner` is missing or empty. All three apps that call it pass their team, and PLAT-103 is closed. CI and CD were both green after the merge.

- **PR:** I opened one PR, mono #1 (`plat-103-require-app-owner`), instead of one per ticket. The shared contract is inlined into the apps at build time, so merging it alone would have broken any app that didn't yet pass `owner`.
- **Shared contract:** I bumped `@mfe/shared-contracts` to 2.0.0 because the change is breaking.
- **Owners:** core-shell passes `platform`, billing passes `payments`, and reports passes `insights`. These match each app's `team` field in `package.json`, but I hardcoded them rather than reading the field.
- **Reports app:** `sub-route-reports` also calls `validateApp` but has no child ticket, so I fixed it in the same PR. CI and CD don't build it, so a missed fix there would only have shown up at runtime.
- **Local builds:** all three apps built locally before I opened the PR.
- **No registry release:** `shared-contracts` lives in the monorepo (`libs/`), so there was nothing to publish or update in the apps' dependencies. I assumed `platform-kit` doesn't call `validateApp`, because a search of the repo found no use of it there.
- **Delays:** the first `sed` edit failed on macOS and changed nothing; I redid it with `perl`. I also had to use the repo key `mono` instead of the repo name for `st clone`.

I marked all four child tickets done and closed the epic with `st done`, including these assumptions.
